hints: Compare the weight components along the planes ($1.6g\sin 50^\circ$ vs $1.2g\sin 40^\circ$) to determine that $B$ tends to move down, meaning friction opposes on both planes.
Find the normal reactions $R_A = 1.2g\cos 40^\circ$ and $R_B = 1.6g\cos 50^\circ$, giving limiting frictions $F_A = \mu R_A$ and $F_B = \mu R_B$.
Write equilibrium equations along each plane: $T = 1.6g\sin 50^\circ - F_B$ and $T = 1.2g\sin 40^\circ + F_A$.
walkthrough:
First, determine the direction of impending motion by comparing the gravitational force components parallel to each incline:
$$\text{For } B:\quad W_{B,\parallel} = m_B g\sin 50^\circ = (1.6)(10)\sin 50^\circ \approx 12.2567\text{ N}$$
$$\text{For } A:\quad W_{A,\parallel} = m_A g\sin 40^\circ = (1.2)(10)\sin 40^\circ \approx 7.7135\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Because } W_{B,\parallel} > W_{A,\parallel},\text{ particle } B \text{ tends to slide down, pulling } A \text{ up.}$$

Consequently, limiting friction acts up the slope on $B$ and down the slope on $A$. Calculate the normal reaction forces perpendicular to each plane:
$$R_A = m_A g\cos 40^\circ = (1.2)(10)\cos 40^\circ = 12\cos 40^\circ$$
$$R_B = m_B g\cos 50^\circ = (1.6)(10)\cos 50^\circ = 16\cos 50^\circ$$

Write the limiting friction expressions using $F = \mu R$:
$$F_A = \mu R_A = 12\mu\cos 40^\circ$$
$$F_B = \mu R_B = 16\mu\cos 50^\circ$$

Formulate the equilibrium equations along each inclined plane:
$$\text{For } B:\quad 16\sin 50^\circ - T - 16\mu\cos 50^\circ = 0 \implies T = 16\sin 50^\circ - 16\mu\cos 50^\circ$$
$$\text{For } A:\quad T - 12\mu\cos 40^\circ - 12\sin 40^\circ = 0 \implies T = 12\sin 40^\circ + 12\mu\cos 40^\circ$$

Equate the two expressions for tension $T$ to eliminate $T$:
$$16\sin 50^\circ - 16\mu\cos 50^\circ = 12\sin 40^\circ + 12\mu\cos 40^\circ$$

Group terms containing $\mu$ on the right and constant terms on the left:
$$16\sin 50^\circ - 12\sin 40^\circ = \mu(12\cos 40^\circ + 16\cos 50^\circ)$$
$$\mu = \frac{16\sin 50^\circ - 12\sin 40^\circ}{12\cos 40^\circ + 16\cos 50^\circ}$$

Evaluate the numerator and denominator:
$$16\sin 50^\circ - 12\sin 40^\circ \approx 12.25671 - 7.71345 = 4.54326$$
$$12\cos 40^\circ + 16\cos 50^\circ \approx 9.19253 + 10.28460 = 19.47713$$
$$\mu = \frac{4.54326}{19.47713} \approx 0.23326$$
$$\mu = 0.233\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$
